editorial:
College decisions are stressing everyone out, and Elle is right in the middle of it. She's trying to keep her long-distance romance with Noah alive while also dealing with changes in her friendship with Lee and a new crush on a classmate named Marco. The vibe is light, teen-focused, and full of drama that feels familiar if you've ever been through high school. You get romance, friendship fights, and plenty of awkward moments that make you smile. It's the kind of movie you put on when you want something easy and fun, not heavy or serious.

The acting is decent, especially from the leads who bring real chemistry to their scenes. The pacing moves quickly, so you won't get bored, though some plot points feel a bit predictable. On the plus side, the friendships feel genuine and the romance has sweet moments. On the downside, the drama can feel over-the-top at times. If you enjoy teen rom-coms, this is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Elle realizes she needs to be honest about her feelings. She breaks things off with Marco after admitting her heart still belongs to Noah. Noah surprises her by showing up, and they reunite. Lee and Elle also patch up their friendship after their big fight. The twist is that Elle gets accepted into a college that lets her stay close to both Noah and Lee, giving everyone a happy ending without anyone having to sacrifice their future.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen rom-coms and friendship drama.
similarMovies: To All the Boys I've Loved Before
